calls.summary: The discussion focused on a significant bug that caused feature activation to occur immediately rather than on the scheduled date, disrupting user experience for restaurants. Damon and Cary identified inconsistencies in how rules can be edited once disabled, complicating management before activation. The role of SDKs in rule activation logic was also addressed, highlighting the need for clarification regarding backend processes. To enhance communication, the team agreed to use Slack for swift updates and escalation of issues to the development team for prompt resolution. Ongoing monitoring and progress updates will be shared via Slack to ensure transparency as they work on fixing the bug.

calls.summary: The meeting provided an overview of GrowthBook's integration with data warehouses such as Snowflake and Databricks, enabling product managers to independently define metrics using SQL queries without extensive coding skills. Feature flags were highlighted for their flexible rollout controls, allowing targeting specific user groups and automatic rollbacks when necessary. Additionally, the platform supports a variety of experiments with statistical analysis while ensuring auto health checks and retroactive metric additions for in-depth evaluations. The organization of projects and tags simplifies feature flag management, allowing the customization of visibility and permissions. SDKs for web and mobile presented caching options to enhance performance, with an emphasis on minimizing API calls. The conversation concluded with next steps for a pilot program focusing on native warehouse integration and ongoing support.
calls.keywords: Feature Flags, Experimentation Platform, Data Warehouse Native, Ramp-up Rollout, Statistical Analysis, SDK Integration

calls.title: cary@growthbook.io - Thu, 04 Jun 2026 12:35:41 EDT - Untitled
calls.summary: The discussion centered on the migration from a self-hosted model to a SaaS platform for GrowthBook, highlighting the unchanged core functionality and data flow of the SDK. The meeting detailed the architecture differences, notably the serving of payloads through GrowthBook’s CDN, while maintaining event data pipelines via Conde’s analytics framework. Support for migration was emphasized, with GrowthBook providing tools and direct contacts like Chris Sanders to facilitate a smooth transition without additional fees. Performance expectations were discussed, with a focus on maintaining or exceeding the current self-hosted metrics of around 250 RPS. Cost implications indicate a potential increase of $15,000 to $20,000, with strategies for seat expansion aimed at better discount negotiations.
calls.keywords: GrowthBook SaaS, Self-hosted migration, CDN latency, MCP server, Experiment platform, Pricing negotiation
